answer: Fixed-pool dilution starves bulk forgery. One nectar pool of 40,000 serves all identities, so each fake shrinks shares. Each identity files one signed claim in the hollow ledger for a 46 nectar fee, locking 70. Each epoch a plume audit samples one in twenty claims; copies burn bonds. 1,000 fakes pay 46,000 and lock 70,000, yet each share is 40, below the 46 fee, so pool-splitting cannot beat it. One honest agent pays 46 once, keeps its share.
